P.text: Launchpad::pairFor calculates pair addresses using uniV2InitCodeHash and a 2-parameter salt (token0, token1), while GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory::createPair deploys pairs using the actual bytecode hash and a 4-parameter salt (token0, token1, launchpadLp, launchpadFeeDistributor)
P.evidence_quote: The factory uses a 4-parameter salt (token0, token1, launchpadLp, launchpadFeeDistributor) while pairFor() only uses 2 parameters (token0, token1).

I.text: pairFor() must use the exact same salt and init code hash that GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory::createPair uses so both resolve to the same CREATE2 address
I.evidence_quote: The pairFor() in Launchpad.sol must use the exact same salt that GTELaunchpadV2PairFactory::createPair uses.

V.text: pairFor() calculates a different address than where the pair is deployed, so _createPairAndSwapRemaining() calls skim() on a non-existent contract and always reverts, causing every token graduation to fail and tokens to get stuck in the bonding phase
V.evidence_quote: This will always revert because it's calling `skim()` on a non-existent contract.
